claims.text: Cerumen impaction is the most common external ear obstruction; it can cause hearing loss, tinnitus, fullness, itching or ear pain.
claims.quote: Cerumen (earwax) impaction is the most common cause of external ear obstruction ( 1 ). It can cause hearing loss, tinnitus, fullness, itching, otalgia, or rarely, ear discharge.

claims.text: Options: cerumenolytics, irrigation and manual removal.
claims.quote: For cerumen , approaches include cerumenolysis, irrigation, and manual removal.

claims.text: Cerumenolytics (eg, hydrogen peroxide, carbamide peroxide, glycerin, docusate, mineral oil) soften very hard wax before removal.
claims.quote: Cerumenolytics, also called cerumen solvents ( hydrogen peroxide , carbamide peroxide , glycerin , triethanolamine, liquid docusate sodium, or mineral oil ), may be used to soften very hard wax before direct removal.

claims.text: Manual removal with a blunt curette, loop, right-angle hook or suction, under good lighting, can be quicker and safer than irrigation.
claims.quote: Cerumen can be removed by rolling it out of the ear canal with a blunt "Buck" curette or loop or a small, blunt right angle hook, or by removing it with a suction tip (eg, Baron, size 5 French). Adequate lighting is essential. These methods, particularly when performed by an experienced clinician, can be quicker and safer than irrigation.

claims.text: Don't irrigate with a known tympanic membrane perforation or a suspected infection.
claims.quote: It is contraindicated in patients with a known tympanic membrane perforation or with a suspected infection.

claims.text: Refer to ENT when impaction blocks the view of the eardrum, when practical.
claims.quote: In general, cerumen impaction that is severe enough to prevent visualization of the eardrum should be managed by an otolaryngologist, when practical.
